answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should charge every identity with work that is cheap once and ruinous at scale. A single mesa check proves almost nothing on its own, yet when that check is tied to a public fable of vouches, penalties and timing, a cluster of fake accounts starts to stand out. Trust then accumulates the way a grove builds: slowly, in the open, and only while the same identity keeps behaving honestly by showing up again and again.
